clue.text: Farewell to the double feature

indicators.note: the word double asks for the feature to be written out twice in a row

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: A goodbye at the end of a cinema's double bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is an informal British toast or goodbye, a cheery parting word.

clue.text: Force thus to give up brandy

indicators.note: in a down clue give up means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape pressings

explanation.surface: Someone is pressured into giving up drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give up' turns MARC upwards in this down clue, giving the letters backwards; 'thus' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to force or stuff something in.

clue.text: Bachelor's brief confession in a line of verse

parts.note: a confession begins 'I am', the admission of what one is
B is the short form of bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: A single man makes a terse admission in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The bachelor confesses 'I am B', the confession itself cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot, a short then long syllable, found within a line of poetry.

clue.text: Business groups somehow making cast iron without oxygen

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some unspecified new order

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Companies manage to produce cast iron without any oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer without oxygen (one O) is an anagram of CAST IRON: so the answer is the letters of CAST IRON plus O, rearranged by 'somehow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Consortia are associations of companies joined for a venture.

clue.text: Fashionable container of French perfume is brilliant

parts.note: in means fashionable
a can is a container
de is French for of
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: A trendy bottle of French perfume is a dazzler.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent means glowing brightly with heat.

clue.text: A plank on a boat

parts.note: a plank is a length of board

explanation.surface: Someone walks the plank aboard a pirate ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard means being carried on a ship or vessel.

clue.text: High economic growth keeps pound in healthy state …

indicators.note: keeps means the economic word holds the pound inside it

parts.note: a boom is a period of rapid economic growth
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Strong growth keeps sterling in good shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in bloom is to be at one's peak, flourishing.

clue.text: … and is often indicated by these signs

definitions.text: and is often indicated by these signs

parts.words: and is often indicated by these signs
parts.note: the word 'and', continued from the previous clue, is often written with a single symbol

explanation.surface: A note that the word and is often shown by symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: The & symbol is a shorthand sign standing for the word and.

clue.text: Daughter is accused but allowed to go

parts.note: charged means formally accused

explanation.surface: A daughter is charged with a crime but released.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone discharged is released, let free from custody or duty.

clue.text: Look back on battle in lists of anniversaries

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the following piece is put after the battle

parts.note: the Alma was a Crimean War battle of 1854

indicators.note: back tells us the word for look is read in reverse order

parts.note: to scan is to look over

explanation.surface: A historian looks back on a battle in a calendar of anniversaries.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alma is a river in Crimea, site of an 1854 battle; 'back' reverses the look word, and 'on' sets it after the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Almanacs are annual calendars listing dates, events and anniversaries.

clue.text: The body of the college

definitions.meaning: Latin for body, used of a body of writings
... Christi is a college at both Oxford and Cambridge, called by its first word

explanation.surface: The governing body of a university college.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is Latin for body and the familiar short name of Corpus Christi College.

clue.text: A fool may be taken -in by this

definitions.text: A fool may be taken -in by this

parts.words: A fool may be taken -in by this
parts.note: taken in reads as deceived, but a fool here is a fruit pudding, eaten with a utensil

explanation.surface: A gullible person may be deceived by some trick.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a creamy fruit dessert such as gooseberry fool; the stray hyphen is a print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This mid-sized spoon is used to eat puddings, including a fruit fool.

clue.text: Token demonstration organised by Duke of York?

parts.note: a counter is a token used in games
a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: A symbolic protest march arranged by a royal duke.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme's Grand Old Duke of York marched his men up the hill and down again: a march reversing its direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A countermarch turns troops back the way they came, exactly the rhyme's up-and-down marching.

clue.text: He demonstrates he's a member of church

definitions.meaning: one who protests or demonstrates against something
an adherent of a Reformed Western Christian church

explanation.surface: A protester is also a churchgoer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word literally means one protesting, and names a member of a Reformation church.

clue.text: Commendation announced for officers and crew

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, so we want one that sounds like it

parts.note: a compliment is an expression of praise

explanation.surface: Praise is publicly given to a ship's officers and sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's complement is its full number of personnel.

clue.text: Little bounder stumped for somewhere to sleep

parts.note: a roo is a kangaroo, a bounding animal, cut short as little suggests
st is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A small cad is dismissed in cricket and looks for a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds settle to sleep.

clue.text: A piece of cake one swallowed during tea, sitting comfortably here

parts.note: something that is a piece of cake is easy

indicators.note: swallowed says the word for tea takes the letter for one inside it

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a slice of cake at teatime, settled comfortably in their seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' puts I inside CHAR, giving CHAIR; 'during' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a soft armchair where one sits in comfort.

clue.text: Dish made from game, with end folded over

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets

indicators.note: folded over means the end is turned back on itself, reading backwards

parts.note: the end here is the last pair of letters of the game word

explanation.surface: A dish made from game birds, its edges folded over like a pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests venison; it is the lawn game. Its end, ET, is folded back as TE and tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a fried roll of minced food in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: One taking striking steps to entertain

definitions.text: One taking striking steps to entertain

parts.words: One taking striking steps to entertain
parts.note: striking steps reads as impressive moves, but means steps that strike the floor with metal plates for a performer's audience

explanation.surface: A performer makes a dazzling entrance to amuse the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: This performer's dance shoes strike the floor audibly, so every step is literally a strike.

clue.text: Veteran hopelessly oiled

indicators.note: hopelessly suggests something gone badly wrong, so the next word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An old soldier is hopelessly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old-timer, someone long experienced.

clue.text: Go to extremes with such sauce

definitions.text: Go to extremes with such sauce

parts.words: Go to extremes with such sauce
parts.note: going to extremes describes a sauce combining two opposite tastes

explanation.surface: A cook overdoes it with a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese-style sauce pairs two opposite flavours, sugar and vinegar, the extremes of taste.

clue.text: He's left the lady on the lake, giving a sort of wave

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the lady above the lake
left means the letters have gone away from the next word

parts.note: taken as the letters he
Ida is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man has abandoned a woman beside a lake, prompting a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's left the': HE leaves THE, leaving T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal wave is a huge wave, hence tidal is a kind of wave.

clue.text: Run and hide

definitions.meaning: an animal's skin with the fur on

explanation.surface: An instruction to flee and conceal oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelt means to dash along, and also an animal skin.

clue.text: Spot googly at last by sixth sense

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is called the sixth sense

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A batsman reads a googly at the last moment by instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: A googly is a cricket delivery that spins the opposite way to what the batsman expects.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of something.

clue.text: A good objective and a plan of action

parts.note: an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A worthy goal and a strategy to reach it.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a programme of things to be done.

clue.text: Port anticipating ship in vain

indicators.note: anticipating means coming before, so the port comes ahead of the ship

parts.note: Bootle is a dock town beside Liverpool on the Mersey
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Harbour officials wait in vain for a ship to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOTLE is a port town on Merseyside in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootless is an old word for unavailing, done to no purpose.

clue.text: Gossip swallowed by Clement Attlee

indicators.note: swallowed by means the letters sit inside the run of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A rumour that the Labour prime minister Clement Attlee heard and kept to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the British Labour prime minister of 1945-51.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattle is idle chatter or tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Can switch to established railway line

indicators.note: switch says the letters of the preceding word change places

explanation.surface: A transport planner wants to switch a service to an existing railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: One's line is one's lineage, the family descent.
